chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad informed me, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
"When you place your hand in the water, then say: In the Name of Allah, and by Allah. O Allah, make me among those who constantly repent, and make me among those who purify themselves,
and when you finish, then say: All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds."

Then he said: "And the wudu (ablution) of the woman is like the wudu (ablution) of the man, equally, except that the sunnah (prophetic tradition) is that the woman should begin, in washing her hands after her face, with the inner side of her forearms, while the man begins with washing the outer side of them."

key_terms.التَّوَّابِينَ: those who repeatedly repent and return to Allah
key_terms.السُّنَّةَ: the recommended prophetic manner or practice
key_terms.الْمُتَطَهِّرِينَ: those who purify themselves ritually and spiritually
key_terms.غَسْلِ: washing as part of the ablution rite
key_terms.وُضُوءُ: ritual ablution before acts of worship

ai.seo_question: What should be said during wudu (ablution), and is a woman’s wudu different from a man’s?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a supplication to be recited at the beginning and end of wudu (ablution), linking ritual purification with tawbah (repentance) and inward purity. It also states that the wudu (ablution) of women and men is the same in ruling, while mentioning a sunnah-based difference in the manner of washing the arms.
